topic: Solving Simultaneous Linear Equations by Elimination

lessonData.topic: Solving Simultaneous Linear Equations by Elimination
lessonData.subject: Mathematics / Algebra
lessonData.tagline: Knock out one variable to conquer the system with precision!
lessonData.overview: The elimination method allows you to solve systems of linear equations by adding or subtracting them to cancel out one unknown variable. By matching coefficients using multiplication across the entire equation, you reduce two complex relationships down to one simple equation you can solve in seconds.

diagram.title: The Elimination Method Workflow
diagram.description: Step-by-step decision pathway for eliminating variables in a linear system

nodes.label: Align & Inspect Coefficients
nodes.sublabel: Check coefficients of x and y
nodes.details: Write equations in standard form (ax + by = c) and inspect whether the coefficients of either variable have identical magnitudes.

nodes.label: Multiply Whole Equations (LCM)
nodes.details: If coefficients differ, multiply one or both full equations by constants using LCM so that one variable has matching or opposite coefficients.

nodes.label: Add or Subtract Equations
nodes.details: Eliminate the target variable. Beware: subtracting negative terms turns them into additions, e.g., 7y - (-6y) = 13y.

nodes.label: Solve Single Variable
nodes.details: Solve the remaining basic linear equation (like 13y = 13 or 47x = 94) to get the value of the first variable.

nodes.label: Substitute & Verify
nodes.details: Substitute the found value into either original equation to solve for the second variable, then check both solutions in the other equation.

chalkNotes.title: Solving Systems: The Elimination Strategy
chalkNotes.subtitle: Balancing equations and avoiding the double-negative trap
chalkNotes.coreRuleOrFormula: Same Sign → Subtract | Opposite Signs → Add | Scale BOTH Sides
bulletPoints: Step 1: Check coefficients. If they match in magnitude, jump to elimination; if not, multiply the ENTIRE equation (both LHS and RHS) by a factor.
Step 2: Watch sign arithmetic: (7y) - (-6y) = 7y + 6y = 13y (subtracting a negative is adding).
Step 3: Add equations when signs are opposite: (-12y) + (+12y) = 0.
Step 4: Once one variable is isolated and solved, substitute it into either original equation to find the second variable.
keyTakeaways: Never forget to multiply the constant on the right-hand side (RHS) when scaling an equation.
Always check your final pair (x, y) by substituting into BOTH original equations.

quiz.question:
A student attempts to solve the system:
(1) 3x + 7y = 17
(2) 3x - 6y = 4
They decide to subtract equation (2) from equation (1) to eliminate x, and write: (3x - 3x) + (7y - 6y) = 17 - 4, leading to y = 13. What fatal error did they make?
options: They failed to distribute the subtraction sign to the negative term: 7y - (-6y) equals 13y, not y.
They should have added the equations instead, because 3x and 3x have the same sign.
They forgot to multiply equation (2) by 3 before subtracting.
They subtracted the right-hand side incorrectly; 17 - 4 equals 21.
quiz.explanation: Subtracting an equation applies a negative sign to every term in that equation. The y-term becomes 7y - (-6y) = 7y + 6y = 13y. The student incorrectly computed 7y - 6y = y. The correct line gives 13y = 13, which means y = 1.

suggestedQuestions: Before eliminating, how do I quickly solve a single variable equation like 13y = 13?
What happens to the equation if I only multiply the terms on the left side of the equals sign?
How do I choose whether it is easier to eliminate x or eliminate y when numbers are large?

annotations.label: Equilibrium Pivot
annotations.description: Represents the equals sign (=); multiplying or modifying one pan requires identical modification of the other.

annotations.description: Contains variable terms (e.g., 13x - 6y) that scale simultaneously.

annotations.label: Right-Hand Side Pan (RHS)
annotations.description: Contains constant terms (e.g., 20) that must also double when LHS is doubled.

solving-simultaneous-linear-equations-by.title: Solving by Elimination Step-by-Step
solving-simultaneous-linear-equations-by.description: A 4-step workflow showing how to eliminate one variable to solve a system of two linear equations.

nodes.label: Align Matching Coefficients
nodes.details: Multiply one or both equations so that coefficients of either x or y become identical or exact opposites.

nodes.label: Add or Subtract Equations
nodes.details: Add equations if coefficients have opposite signs, or subtract if they have matching signs, eliminating one variable.

nodes.label: Solve for First Variable
nodes.details: Solve the resulting single-variable equation using basic inverse operations to find its numerical value.

nodes.label: Back-Substitute for Second Variable
nodes.details: Substitute the found value back into either original equation to calculate the other variable and form the solution pair (x, y).

key-properties-of-solving-simultaneous-l.title: Core Steps of the Elimination Method
key-properties-of-solving-simultaneous-l.description: How to eliminate one variable by matching coefficients and combining equations to find the solution pair (x, y).

nodes.label: Match Coefficients
nodes.details: Multiply one or both equations by a constant so that one variable has equal or opposite coefficients.

nodes.label: Add or Subtract Equations
nodes.sublabel: Opposite signs add, same signs subtract
nodes.details: Combine the two equations vertically to cancel out the targeted variable completely.

nodes.label: Solve for First Variable
nodes.details: Solve the resulting single-variable equation using basic inverse operations.

nodes.label: Back-Substitute to Find (x, y)
nodes.details: Substitute the found value back into either original equation to determine the second variable.

nodes.label: Event Ticket Sales

contrast:rhs-unmultiplied-scaling.checkQuestion: To keep an equation balanced, whatever operation you do to the left-hand side must also be done to what?

steps.name: Original Equation
steps.caption: Let's start with our balanced equation: 13x - 6y = 20.

steps.name: Testing the rule
steps.caption: If we multiply by 2, what happens if we only change the left side?

steps.name: The visual clash
steps.caption: Because 26x - 12y is not equal to 20, the equality breaks.

steps.name: The working rule
steps.caption: To keep the balance, we must multiply every term by 2, including the right side.

steps.name: Check understanding

contrast:rhs-unmultiplied-scaling.focus: Multiplying an equation by a constant only applies to the terms on the left-hand side.
